role: Phase 3F.1-terminal Part A - production fix for exactly this one defect.

reproductionInherited.certifiedWorkingAlready: The core operative? disclose-status : fallback gating Workstream B's earlier BLOCKER-5 fix added to getDefinition is real and correct: a query using the term's own EXACT canonical (already-normalized) spelling always got the right disclosure for CONFLICTED/PARTIAL/RESOLVED-after-a-chain states, and the 'multiple candidate definitions' (never-amended base-document collision) invariant genuinely held even under adversarial pressure.
reproductionInherited.theGap: getDefinition's term-lookup helper (findProvisionView in semantic/tools.ts) compared the queried term with only `.trim().toLowerCase()` - leading/trailing whitespace only - unlike its own SECTION-branch sibling on the same line (`.replace(/\s+/g, "")`, full whitespace collapse) and unlike normalizeDefinedTermRef (amendment/chain.ts), the exact function already used to STORE OperativeProvisionView.definedTermRef in the first place. A query term with irregular INTERNAL whitespace (a doubled space, a tab, a line-wrap remnant - realistic artifacts of an LLM echoing a term name read from real, often OCR'd/line-wrapped contract text) silently missed a real, on-file OperativeProvisionView and fell through to the base-document fallback, re-serving stale pre-amendment text labeled OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED for exactly the two operative-state classes the fallback's own ambiguity check (resolveUniqueDefinitionByRef) cannot independently re-catch: OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED (two same-date competing effects) and OPERATIVE_STATE_PARTIAL via textMissingDespiteAppliedEffect (a real applied effect with no capturable replacement text).
reproductionInherited.whyThisMatters: This is a verbatim recurrence of the exact defect class the earlier BLOCKER-5/6 fix was meant to close, reachable only because that fix's own required test always queried with the term's canonical, already-single-spaced form and never tried a whitespace-variant query - the fix closed the gate but never audited the term-matching helper the gate's own first branch depends on to fire at all.

rootCauseFix.change: The DEFINITION-branch comparison now normalizes BOTH sides via normalizeDefinedTermRef (imported from amendment/operative-state.ts's own re-export) instead of `ref.trim().toLowerCase()` vs. a bare `.toLowerCase()` on the stored field - mirroring the SECTION-branch neighbor's own full-whitespace-collapse discipline rather than inventing a second, parallel normalization rule, exactly as the recertification's own recommendedFix named. Fixes the shared helper for every one of its callers (getOperativeProvision, getRelatedAmendments, getPriorVersion, resolveNodeWithSupersessionAwareness), not merely getDefinition's own reproduction.
rootCauseFix.note: getDefinition itself no longer routes through findProvisionView at all (see architecturalFix below) - this fix is retained anyway because findProvisionView is still the live lookup for getRelatedAmendments/getPriorVersion/getOperativeProvision, all of which shared the identical whitespace gap for any DEFINITION-kind ref they were queried with.

architecturalFix.summary: Unified definition access behind one canonical primitive - resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence (lib/contract-model/compiler/amendment/operative-state.ts) - reused verbatim by both getDefinition (semantic/tools.ts) and getTargetCurrentText (amendment/pipeline.ts), replacing two independently-maintained temporal disciplines with one.

statusEnum.name: DefinitionEvidenceStatus

values.CURRENT: Confidently current, safe to treat as settled fact - either a fully-resolved amendment chain, or a genuinely never-amended, uniquely-resolved base-document definition with no known supersession. isCurrentTruth=true ONLY for this status.
values.KNOWN_SUPERSEDED: A real, disclosed NodeSupersessionIndex record shows this exact physical base-document occurrence no longer governs, even though no DEFINITION-kind amendment effect targeted the TERM itself (e.g. its enclosing section was independently replaced by a SECTION-kind amendment). NEW capability - the base-document fallback previously never checked supersession at all for definitions, unlike every SECTION-reading tool.
values.OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED: A real, on-file amendment conflict (OPERATIVE_STATE_CONFLICTED) or an otherwise review-required chain state - no confident current text exists and none is fabricated.
values.AMBIGUOUS_TARGET: 2+ real, colliding physical definitions/candidates and no way to pick one without guessing - never guessed. Reachable both via a real amendment effect whose own target collides (view.targetResolutionStatus AMBIGUOUS, disclosed - not refused) and via the no-recorded-amendment fallback (refused outright, since there is no amendment evidence to disclose alongside the collision).
values.PARTIAL_AMENDMENT: A real, resolved, dated effect governs this exact term but supplied no capturable replacement text (textMissingDespiteAppliedEffect).
values.HISTORICAL_ONLY: A real amendment references this term but its own base-document target could not be confirmed to exist at all (targetResolutionStatus NOT_FOUND) - the amendment's own claimed text (attemptedText) is disclosed for context, explicitly labeled historical/unconfirmed, never presented as current.

statusEnum.isCurrentTruth: Boolean companion field, true iff status === CURRENT - the single field a downstream caller should gate on rather than string-matching every status value.
statusEnum.legacyStatus: A second field, `legacyStatus`, echoes the pre-existing OperativeStateStatus vocabulary (OPERATIVE_STATE_RESOLVED/PARTIAL/CONFLICTED/REVIEW_REQUIRED) verbatim from the underlying OperativeProvisionView.status (or the pre-existing RESOLVED/PARTIAL convention for the two base-document-fallback outcomes) - added specifically for backward compatibility with already-committed tests (tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-blocker2-6-tools-adversarial.test.ts, tests/contract-model/finding-2-3-getDefinition-operative-safety-e2e.test.ts) that assert on getDefinition's own `status` field using that exact vocabulary. getDefinition's tool response exposes BOTH: `status` (legacy, unchanged wire shape) and the new `evidenceStatus`/`isCurrentTruth` fields.

architecturalFix.designDecisionAmbiguousDisclosureNotRefu: A real, on-file OperativeProvisionView whose own targetResolutionStatus is AMBIGUOUS is DISCLOSED (outcome FOUND, ok:true, status/evidenceStatus/unresolvedIssues populated, text withheld as "(no current text recorded)") rather than refused - mirroring getOperativeProvision's own established discipline (a found view is always disclosed, never refused; only the SEPARATE no-view-at-all fallback ever refuses on ambiguity). An earlier draft of this fix made the view-AMBIGUOUS case a hard refusal and was caught regressing tests/contract-model/part-b-recert-blocker2-6-tools-adversarial.test.ts's own frozen fixture before being corrected.
architecturalFix.whitespaceRobustnessBeyondTheOneLineFix: resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence's own term-lookup normalizes BOTH the query and the stored OperativeProvisionView.definedTermRef via normalizeDefinedTermRef at the comparison site (never trusting the stored field was already normalized) - this is what actually fixed several already-committed hand-built test fixtures (which set definedTermRef to the term's original, un-normalized casing) in addition to closing the whitespace-variant-query reproduction; the same defensive both-sides-normalize discipline was applied to findProvisionView's own DEFINITION branch for the same reason.
architecturalFix.pipelineTsIntegration: amendment/pipeline.ts's getTargetCurrentText (used to feed interpretAmendmentClause's own LLM call with an amendment target's 'current text' context) now calls resolveOperativeDefinitionEvidence with operativeState: null (deliberate - no OperativeContractState exists yet at this pipeline stage, since this function runs WHILE amendment effects are still being discovered, before operative state can be computed from them) and searchDocumentIds: [target.targetDocumentId] (the single already-resolved target document, never widened). Behavior for AMBIGUOUS/NOT_FOUND is unchanged (both still yield null); the UNIQUE case now automatically gains definition-supersession awareness for free, though no NodeSupersessionIndex exists at this pipeline stage today so this call site's real answer is unaffected in practice - the unification is architectural (one primitive, not two), not a behavior change here.
architecturalFix.supersessionCheckDetail: The base-document (no-recorded-amendment) fallback now checks the resolved definition's own sourceNodeId against this compilation's real NodeSupersessionIndex (already built once per attempt in buildToolSet, reused - never a second computation) via getNodeSupersessionStatus. Because detectStructuralDefinitions anchors a definition's sourceNodeId to its ENCLOSING structural node (not a synthetic per-term node), a definition that was never individually targeted by a DEFINITION-kind amendment effect can still be correctly flagged KNOWN_SUPERSEDED when its enclosing section was independently replaced by a SECTION-kind amendment - closing a gap symmetric to the original SUPER-5 finding (getDefinition's base-document fallback was the one remaining evidence tool never wired to supersession awareness).

downstreamPropagation.designPrinciple: A semantic compiler using an unresolved definition may still produce candidate IR for review, but must not become trusted verified current truth solely from that definition - enforced deterministically (never relying on the model's own self-reported sufficiency alone), by threading one new boolean signal through the existing, already-built architecture rather than rewiring semantic-coverage/safe-failure directly.

signal.semantics: true iff a CURRENT_OPERATIVE_EVIDENCE-discipline tool call's own returned evidence has isCurrentTruth===false (a real conflict/partial/ambiguous-target/known-superseded/historical-only result) - undefined for refusals and for tools this does not apply to. Set on getDefinition's own outcome; carried onto the ToolRunner's logged entry unconditionally, never re-derived from outputSummary text.

compileTs.change: compileCovenantToIR now pushes the existing SemanticCompilerFailureReason "OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED" onto failureReasons whenever ANY toolCallLog entry from this attempt carries evidenceUnresolved:true - independent of, and in addition to, the pre-existing model-self-reported-sufficiency check. determineStatus already treats any non-empty failureReasons as at least REVIEW_REQUIRED (never silently upgraded to COMPLETED merely because ruleCount>0), so this attempt-level status can no longer be COMPLETED off a dishonestly-reported COMPLETE sufficiency alone.

verifyTs.change: verifyCompiledCandidate's determineStatus now also returns REVIEW_REQUIRED whenever compilationResult.toolCallLog shows an unresolved-evidence entry (hasUnresolvedDefinitionEvidence helper) - placed in the same priority tier as the existing operativeLineage CONFLICTED/REVIEW_REQUIRED and KNOWN_SUPERSEDED checks, i.e. before any clean VERIFIED_* result can be returned. This closes the DEPENDENCY-definition gap the pre-existing checks did not cover: operativeLineage only ever describes the candidate's OWN provision text, never a definition it merely relied on for meaning via a getDefinition call mid-compilation.

downstreamPropagation.cascadeToAlreadyBuiltDownstreamArchitect: No changes were needed in semantic-coverage/ or safe-failure/ - both already gate off verifyCompiledCandidate's own status via already-existing wiring: analysis/orchestrator.ts's verifiedCandidateRefs only includes candidateRefs whose verification status is VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND/VERIFIED_WITH_NON_MATERIAL_FINDINGS (now correctly excluding a tainted candidate); semantic-coverage/reconciliation.ts's own `verified = coveringCandidates.some((c) => input.verifiedCandidateRefs.has(...))` downgrades such a unit from FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED to FULLY_REPRESENTED_REVIEW_REQUIRED; analysis/semantic-truth/mapping.ts's computeTrustStatus maps a non-VERIFIED_* verification status to trustStatus REVIEW_REQUIRED (never VERIFIED), so the persisted SemanticTruthRecord is correctly downgraded; and safe-failure/derive.ts already treats every coverage state except FULLY_REPRESENTED_VERIFIED as a genuine review gap, emitting a ClaimReviewItem. The fix's two touch points (compile.ts, verify.ts) were sufficient to make the entire already-built chain honest.

testsAdded.note: Not deleted, per instruction. The 4 tests originally written to assert the BUG's own effects (2 'ADVERSARIAL' tests, 1 divergence-check, both inside the CONFLICTED/PARTIAL describe blocks) were updated in place to assert the FIXED, correct behavior - same fixtures, same adversarial query-term construction, opposite (now-correct) expected outcome, with each test's own name/comment updated to say so explicitly. The SETUP CHECK/CONTROL/positive-control tests were left untouched (they were never testing the bug).
newScenarios: no-operative-state case (positive path): operativeState entirely null, a unique never-amended term resolves confidently CURRENT/RESOLVED/source base-document (the existing file already covered the null-operativeState AMBIGUOUS-refusal case; this adds the CURRENT-resolution positive path under the same condition).

AMBIGUOUS amendment: a real, on-file amendment effect targets a term that itself collides across 2 physical base-document definitions (view.targetResolutionStatus AMBIGUOUS) - getDefinition discloses evidenceStatus AMBIGUOUS_TARGET/isCurrentTruth false and withholds every candidate figure, never refusing (a real view exists).

superseded definition: a term never individually amended, but its own enclosing structural node ('Section 1.01 Definitions') was independently superseded by a whole-section REPLACE_TEXT amendment - getDefinition's base-document fallback now checks the real NodeSupersessionIndex and labels it KNOWN_SUPERSEDED, never CURRENT/RESOLVED-as-if-never-amended.

historical retrieval correctly labeled as historical, never as current: a real amendment references a term whose own base-document target could not be confirmed to exist at all (targetResolutionStatus NOT_FOUND) - getDefinition surfaces the amendment's own claimed text (attemptedText) for context but with evidenceStatus HISTORICAL_ONLY and isCurrentTruth false, never CURRENT.

'multiple physical definition occurrences' and 'partial amendment' were already covered by the pre-existing SETUP CHECK/CONTROL tests in this file (now additionally asserting the new evidenceStatus/isCurrentTruth fields) - not duplicated with new fixtures.

end-to-end (compile.ts): a real RealSemanticCaller + real ToolRunner/getDefinition tool-use loop against a real CONFLICTED fixture, with a scripted model that DISHONESTLY reports sufficiency COMPLETE for the disclosed-conflicted term - proves result.status is deterministically forced to REVIEW_REQUIRED (never COMPLETED) via failureReasons containing OPERATIVE_STATE_UNRESOLVED, independent of the model's own dishonest self-report.

end-to-end (verify.ts): a compiled candidate whose own toolCallLog carries one evidenceUnresolved:true entry, with zero reconciliation findings and skipSemanticReview:true - proves verifyCompiledCandidate's status is REVIEW_REQUIRED, never VERIFIED_NO_MATERIAL_GAP_FOUND/VERIFIED_WITH_NON_MATERIAL_FINDINGS.
